human_tolerance.notes: A familiar bird of deciduous and mixed woodland that readily uses nest boxes and comes to winter feeders, and one of the boldest small birds around people.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: Winter flocks form strict dominance hierarchies and include other bird species; individuals can lower their body temperature during cold winter nights to conserve energy.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Pairs form in late autumn and winter and disperse from the winter flocks in spring; nests in tree cavities 1-7 m above ground, with the female building the nest and both sexes excavating the cavity; six to eight eggs, one brood a year with second broods possible after loss of the first.

phases.name: caching
phases.note: Food caching for the winter; the hippocampus grows during the caching season, which is believed to help the bird remember its cache locations.

vocalizations.description: The two-note fee-bee whistle, particularly given by males: a simple, clear whistle of two identical-rhythm notes, the first roughly a whole step above the second.
The chick-a-dee-dee-dee call, from which the species gets its name; also an explosive snake-like hiss from an incubating female at an unusual disturbance at the nest entrance.

taxonomy.note: GBIF backbone gives family Paridae and authority (Linnaeus, 1766); ITIS scientific-name search returns TSN 554382 with the same authority. The species was long placed in the genus Parus (EltonTraits still files it there); Poecile is the current placement.

external.note: GBIF usageKey 2487805 from species/match; ITIS TSN 554382 from the ITIS scientific-name search; NCBI taxon id 48891, eBird code bkcchi and IUCN category least concern (Q211005) from Wikidata P685, P3444 and P141.

common_names.note: English label from Wikidata Q282687; French label 'Mésange à tête noire' from the same item. No Spanish vernacular is recorded on the item, so none is written here.

range.note: 'They range from western Alaska, through southern Yukon and throughout the Canadian provinces, from British Columbia in the west to the Maritimes and Newfoundland in the east. The distribution continues into the United States'.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Hop and Walk are an authored reading of a small passerine's ground and branch movement; the source describes a bird that 'live and feed in dense vegetation' and hops and flits between twigs without naming gaits, and EltonTraits places foraging in the understory and midhigh strata. Fly is powered.

traits.nest_type.note: 'The black-capped chickadee nests in tree cavities 1-7 m above ground', either excavated by the pair, a natural cavity, or a reused woodpecker hole or nest box.

traits.perching.note: Perches in dense vegetation to feed and roost; nests in cavities and low branches.

traits.senses.note: hearing High from '16 distinct types of vocalizations being used to convey an array of information'; olfaction set Low, no sourced claim found. vision_color authored from the black, white and buff plumage contrast the species is identified by.

traits.size_class.note: From mass_kg (0.0108 kg falls in the Tiny band, under 0.05 kg).

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits BodyMass-Value 10.8 g (under the older name Parus atricapillus) and AVONET Mass 10.8 g agree exactly, both sourced to Dunning 2008, and sit inside Wikipedia's 'Both sexes weigh 10-14 g'.

traits.length_m.note: Authored estimate, and an honest gap: no openly licensed source consulted gives a total bill-tip-to-tail-tip length. Wikipedia's Description section gives only component measurements (bill 8-9.5 mm, tail 56.3-63 mm, tarsus 16-17 mm, wing 60.5-67.5 mm) and AVONET likewise reports culmen, tail, tarsus and wing but no total. 0.13 m is the order-of-magnitude total length implied by summing the culmen, the tail and a trunk of roughly 55-60 mm, which is consistent with a 10-14 g chickadee. Treat as a placeholder rather than a measurement.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Derived, and an honest gap: no openly licensed source consulted states a wingspan. AVONET gives a wing chord of 64.4 mm for this species; 0.135 m is that chord multiplied by 2.1, the usual ratio of spread wingspan to wing chord for a small rounded-wing passerine. The multiplier is a judgement, so treat the value as an approximation, not a measurement.

traits.lifespan_y.note: 'Maximum recorded lifespan is 12 years, although most live roughly 2.5 years'.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-Inv 60, Diet-Fruit 20, Diet-Seed 20, matching 'It feeds primarily on insects and seeds, and is known for its ability to cache food for use during the winter'.

traits.social.note: 'The black-capped chickadee is a social bird and forms strict dominance hierarchies within its flock. During the winter, these flocks include other bird species'; pairs are monogamous for the breeding season, so Flock is the primary year-round structure and the 2-12 band is authored from the winter-flock description.

traits.defense.note: Authored: the species is primarily subject to predation by birds of prey and flushes to cover when threatened; the only explicitly described defence is the incubating female's snake-like hiss at the nest entrance, which is a nest-Entrance threat response rather than the species' main reaction, so Flee is used.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: a bold, familiar bird that uses nest boxes and winter feeders, and is one of the least shy small birds around people.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat-understory 20 + ForStrat-midhigh 80 (100) gives the primary stratum as arboreal; the ground share of 0.2 is authored judgement for the ground-level foraging and food-caching described in the same sections.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Nests and roosts in tree cavities.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet exactly. Nesting weight 1.0 on cavity follows the nesting description. Perch and leaf_litter shelter weights are authored judgement; no open source quantifies their relative use.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Nest-box use is stated in the source ('This species will also nest in a nest box'); willingness to forage in human-modified woodland and the boldness described elsewhere in the article are the basis for Adapter, and light_max is authored (judgement).

seasonal.strategy.note: 'Black-capped chickadees are non-migratory and can be found throughout much of North America.'

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding window from 'the nesting season starting in late April and lasting until late June'; winter flocking from the flock-hierarchy and cold-night torpor paragraphs; caching window is judgement, tied to the autumn food-caching described. Exact window edges are judgements informed by those dates.

seasonal.life_stages.note: 'Young leave the nest 12-16 days after hatching ... The young are still fed by the parents for several weeks, but are capable of catching food on their own within a week after leaving the nest' and 'First breeding is at one year of age', giving a juvenile stage to roughly three months; scale is authored judgement and the egg stage carries no duration because none is sourced.

vocalizations.song.note: The two-note fee-bee whistle from the Vocalization section, which also gives the frequency detail: 'The frequency of their songs typically starts around 400 Hz, and various tones spanning roughly 1 kHz are sung within the song.'

vocalizations.alarm.note: The chick-a-dee-dee-dee call, named in the lead paragraph, plus the incubating female's 'explosive hiss like that of a snake' at the nest entrance.

vocalizations.note: Descriptions, contexts and the frequency band from the Vocalization section; months, time windows and cooldowns are authored judgement, since no open source quantifies them.

look.note: Colours from the Description section (black cap and bib, white cheeks, white underparts with buff flanks, greenish-grey back, slate-grey tail and wings, black beak and legs); the whole head is coloured from the markings slot so the cap reads as black, and the flank tone is carried in the accent slot. Proportions are authored judgement for a small, big-headed, short-beaked chickadee.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program. flee_m kept short (5 m) for a small, bold bird; nest_m1/nest_m2 set to the late-April to late-June nesting season described in the source.
